title: Government Assistance for Residents who are Not Digitally Literate
what_it_is: Government Assistance for Residents who are Not Digitally Literate

sections.label: SG Digital Office and digital inclusion
sections.summary: The SG Digital Office, set up in June 2020, supports less digitally savvy residents through community hubs, ServiceSG Centres and various outreach channels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The SG Digital Office was established in June 2020 to support the adoption of basic digital tools and skills among less digitally savvy individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Residents can visit SG Digital community hubs at selected libraries and community centres to receive one-to-one or small group training on skills, such as how to use a smartphone, make e-payments and learn cybersecurity tips on how to stay safe online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To date, more than 210,000 seniors have been engaged under the Seniors Go Digital Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Public Service has also set up five ServiceSG Centres to serve as one-stop physical touchpoints where officers can guide residents through digital transactions and help them complete frequently used Government services across 20 agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On top of newspaper publications and broadcasts via free-to-air television and radio, many Government agencies inform residents of key policy announcements through hard copy letters, via the Digital Display Panels at HDB blocks and even through house visits.

sections.label: IMDA and PA Community Centres
sections.summary: Through an IMDA-PA partnership, 38 Community Centres offer a scaled-down version of ServiceSG services, helping residents with over 200 services.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The alternative is that through a partnership between IMDA and the People's Association (PA), there are 38 Community Centres that offer a scaled down version of what is available at the ServiceSG Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To give the Member a sense of the scale that ServiceSG Centres are able to help residents with, in terms of services, each one of these ServiceSG Centres, typically, will be able to work with the residents to go through more than upwards of 400 types of services offered by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The 38 Community Centres where there is a partnership between IMDA and PA, they also offer upwards of 200 services that they can help residents to complete.
